name: Full-Panel Setup Deck
note: A y-mandatory snap container holds four full-height panels with scroll-snap-stop:always, while an IntersectionObserver rooted to that scroller drives the side dot rail, the counter and the Next button.
html:
Beacon setup 1 / 4
Step 01

Connect a repository

Point Beacon at a GitHub or GitLab remote. Access stays read-only until you widen it.

Takes about 40 seconds
Step 02

Choose your checks

Thirty-four rules covering leaked secrets, licence drift and stale dependencies.

12 enabled by default
Step 03

Set the merge gate

Block anything above your risk threshold, or annotate the diff and let humans decide.

Recommended: warn first
Step 04

Invite the team

Findings land inline on the pull request, so nobody opens a second tab to triage.

Free for the first 5 seats

name: Snapping Company Timeline
note: Entries snap to the scroll-padded start edge of a y-proximity scroller, and an IntersectionObserver rooted to it expands the focused card from grid-template-rows 0fr to 1fr while the rail fill tracks scrollTop.
html:
How we got here 2019
Mar 2019Seed

Two engineers, one warehouse

Built the first router on a folding table. Shipped 40 units to friendly customers.

Sep 2020Product

Mesh firmware goes public

Open-sourced the radio stack. 1,900 forks in the first month.

Jun 2021Series A

$14M to build the factory

Moved assembly in-house in Porto and cut lead time from 11 weeks to 9 days.

Feb 2023Scale

100,000 nodes online

Coverage across 31 countries, with a median hop latency of 8 ms.

Nov 2025Today

Community-run backbone

Two thirds of traffic now rides relays owned by the people using them.

name: Vertical Story Reel
note: Full-bleed stories fill a y-mandatory snap scroller and an IntersectionObserver rooted to it fills the segment bar, swaps the byline and drives the Next control.
html:
Day 3 · Kyoto

Bamboo before sunrise

Arashiyama at 05:40. Empty for eleven minutes, then the first bus arrived.

Day 3 · Nishiki

Breakfast standing up

Grilled eel on a stick, 480 yen, eaten in the eight steps between stalls.

Day 4 · Osaka

Rain on the arcade roof

Two hours of it. Everyone kept shopping and nobody opened an umbrella.

Day 4 · Koyasan

Cedars the width of cars

Walked the Okunoin path at dusk. Lanterns every ten metres, no other footsteps.

Day 5 · Setouchi

Ferry, last one out

Twenty-two minutes across flat water, sun going down behind the cranes.

MK mika.walks 6h ago
